answer: One strong defence is stake-bonded reputation: an agent must lock a deposit that grows with the value it handles, and that deposit is slashed if peers catch it running duplicate identities. A fake identity is like a relic left in a meadow - it looks old and trusted until someone checks the ground beneath it. Honest agents build history in one open lagoon of attestations, so a Sybil farm must pay the same bond for every clone, and cloning stops being profitable once the bond exceeds the reward.
